answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that scales with identity count. Each new agent must escrow a bond larger than one epoch's expected payout, released only after five established non-kin peers attest its work. A farmer minting ten thousand keys owes ten thousand bonds, and every clone still needs independent attested history before its escrow unlocks, so the farm turns unprofitable long before it grows large. The bond, not the key, carries the risk: a failed attestation slashes it. Trust must precipitate slowly, like umber pigment crystallizing on a wharf beam, never in bulk.
